'''Kaumudi Jinraj Joshipura''' is an Indian American [[Epidemiology|epidemiologist]], [[Biostatistics|biostatistician]] and [[dentist]]. She is Susmita & Subroto Bagchi Professor of Public Health Dean, Bagchi School of Public Health, and Adjunct Full Professor at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (HSPH) at [[Harvard University]] and NIH Endowed Chair and Director of the Center for Clinical Research and Health Promotion and a Full Professor at the [[University of Puerto Rico, Medical Sciences Campus]]. Her research work has been covered by global media including CNN, ABC, NBC, NHS, Newsweek, Nature, Telegraph, Japanese Journals and Japanese TV etc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robertglatter/2017/11/26/regular-use-of-mouthwash-may-increase-risk-for-diabetes/|title=Regular Use Of Mouthwash May Increase Risk For Diabetes|first=Robert Glatter|last=MD|website=Forbes}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.newsweek.com/mouthwash-may-trigger-diabetes-if-you-use-way-way-too-much-it-720931 |title=Mouthwash May Trigger Diabetes—If You Use Way, Way Too Much of It |last=Sheridan |first=Kate |date=23 November 2017 |website= www.newsweek.com|access-date=2020-07-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oasisdiscussions.ca/2017/12/18/mw/|title=Does over-the-counter mouthwash put you at risk of pre-diabetes/diabetes?|date=December 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/lifestyle/health/using-mouthwash-twice-day-could-11567348|title=Why using mouthwash could raise your risk of getting diabetes|first=Adam|last=Aspinall|date=November 22, 2017|website=mirror}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Joshipura |first1=Kaumudi J. |last2=Muñoz-Torres |first2=Francisco J. |last3=Morou-Bermudez |first3=Evangelia |last4=Patel |first4=Rakesh P. |title=Over-the-counter mouthwash use and risk of pre-diabetes/diabetes |journal=Nitric Oxide |date=1 December 2017 |volume=71 |pages=14–20 |doi=10.1016/j.niox.2017.09.004 |pmid=28939409 |pmc=6628144 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/mouthwash-twice-a-day-puts-diabetes-risk-50-per-cent-higher-a3699791.html|title=Mouthwash twice a day 'puts diabetes risk 50 per cent higher'|date=November 23, 2017|website=Evening Standard}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.today.com/health/study-links-mouthwash-diabetes-risk-what-you-need-know-t119320|title=Could mouthwash put you at risk for diabetes? What you need to know|website=TODAY.com|date=29 November 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.medpagetoday.com/reading-room/endocrine-society/diabetes/71148|title=Powerful Connections Between Oral Health and Diabetes Care|date=February 14, 2018|website=www.medpagetoday.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/HEALTH/9910/05/stroke.fruit/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714160451/http://edition.cnn.com/HEALTH/9910/05/stroke.fruit/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 14, 2020|title=CNN - Fruits and vegetables may reduce risk of stroke - October 5, 1999|website=CNN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/08/05/health/oral-hygiene-may-help-more-than-teeth-and-gums.html|title=Oral Hygiene May Help More Than Teeth and Gums|first=Susan|last=Gilbert|newspaper=The New York Times|date=August 5, 2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hZ87XVV7tIk|title=Video |website=www.youtube.com |date=10 November 2015 |accessdate=2020-07-18}}</ref>

== Early life, education, and career ==
Joshipura earned an M.S. in Biostatistics from [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] in 1989. She worked as a staff associate in Biostatistics at [[The Forsyth Institute]] from 1989 to 1992. Joshipura was a clinical instructor in Oral Health Policy and Epidemiology at [[Harvard School of Dental Medicine]] (HSDM) from 1992 to 1993. As a postdoctoral dentist scientist, she completed a postdoctoral fellowship in the Department of Oral Health Policy and Epidemiology (OHPE) at HSDM from 1993 to 1995 during which time she completed a certificate in Dental Public Health at HSDM and a Sc.D. in Epidemiology at the Harvard School of Public Health.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://cdn1.sph.harvard.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/411/2017/02/Joshipura-HSPH_CV_Feb_2017.pdf|title=CV|last=Joshipura|first=Kaumudi Jinraj|date=February 2017|website=Harvard School of Public Health|access-date=|archive-date=2019-09-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190927014300/https://cdn1.sph.harvard.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/411/2017/02/Joshipura-HSPH_CV_Feb_2017.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her dissertation titled ''Oral Health, Nutrition, and Coronary Heart Disease'' was completed under Dr. [[Walter Willett]] in 2 academic semesters including qualifying exam and Doctoral Thesis.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Oral health, nutrition, and coronary heart disease|date=1995|language=English|first=Kaumudi Jinraj|last=Joshipura|oclc=79164739}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1996 to 2002, Joshipura was an Assistant Professor of Epidemiology at Harvard School of Public Health. She was an associate professor in HSDM from 2002 to 2005 and has continued as an Adjunct Full Professor of Epidemiology at Harvard School of Public Health. In 2005, she joined the faculty at [[University of Puerto Rico School of Dental Medicine]], as Professor and Director of Division of Dental Public Health. Since 2007, she serves as the NIH Endowed Chair, Professor, and the Director of the Center for Clinical Research and Health Promotion at the [[University of Puerto Rico, Medical Sciences Campus]].<ref name=":1" /> She has also taught Software Engineering Courses to Advance Engineering Department at Northeastern University and at companies. She has also served as Advisor to AAP and Consultant to WHO, NIH, CDC, Unilever, AADR, Medopad etc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ccrhp.rcm.upr.edu/?q=joshipura|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200710185655/http://ccrhp.rcm.upr.edu/?q=joshipura|archive-date = 2020-07-10|title = Kaumudi Joshipura (B.D.S., MS, SCD) &#124; Center for Clinical Research and Health Promotion (CCRHP)}}</ref> She focuses on identifying and promoting no cost, low cost or cost saving ways to improve health and wellness.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ccrhp.rcm.upr.edu/ |title=Message from the Director &#124; Center for Clinical Research and Health Promotion (CCRHP) |website=ccrhp.rcm.upr.edu |access-date=14 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406180900/http://ccrhp.rcm.upr.edu/ |archive-date=6 April 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> She launched a free global movement to help people overcome inhibitions and barriers to move more throughout the day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vmovement.org/|title=Activating a move-friendly world|website=vmovement|access-date=2020-07-14|archive-date=2020-08-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813103754/https://www.vmovement.org/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCdsSzNGxn1ewrDmy5FhPWng|title=VMovement - YouTube|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

=== Research ===
Joshipura researches lifestyle and other risk factors for cardio-metabolic conditions, and the interrelationships of microbial, dietary, and inflammatory mediators.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Kaumudi_Joshipura |title=Bio|website= www.researchgate.net|access-date=2020-07-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XapbCAAAQBAJ&q=dr.+kaumudi+joshipura&pg=PT407|title=Sodium Bicarbonate|first=Dr Mark|last=Sircus|date=August 5, 2014|publisher=Lulu Press, Inc|isbn=9781312412149|via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Michaud |first1=Dominique S |last2=Liu |first2=Yan |last3=Meyer |first3=Mara |last4=Giovannucci |first4=Edward |last5=Joshipura |first5=Kaumudi |title=Periodontal disease, tooth loss, and cancer risk in male health professionals: a prospective cohort study |journal=The Lancet Oncology |date=June 2008 |volume=9 |issue=6 |pages=550–558 |doi=10.1016/S1470-2045(08)70106-2 |pmid=18462995 |pmc=2601530 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Knapton |first1=Sarah |title=Mouthwash may kill beneficial bacteria in mouth and trigger diabetes, Harvard study suggests |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2017/11/22/mouthwash-may-kill-beneficial-bacteria-mouth-trigger-diabetes/ |work=The Telegraph |date=22 November 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Tooth Loss Linked to Increased Stroke Risk |journal=The Journal of the American Dental Association |date=February 2003 |volume=134 |issue=2 |pages=156–158 |doi=10.14219/jada.archive.2003.0124 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com.pr/citations?user=dqotcHcAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Dr. Kaumudi Joshipura - Google Scholar|website=scholar.google.com.pr|access-date=2020-07-14|archive-date=2023-01-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111165010/https://scholar.google.com.pr/citations?user=dqotcHcAAAAJ&hl=en|url-status=dead}}</ref> She researched the relationship between periodontitis and coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke, and peripheral artery disease. Joshipura has been awarded several NIH grants as the [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]]. Recent grants include SOALS: San Juan Overweight Adults Longitudinal Study, PEARLS: Pregnancy and EARly Lifestyle improvement Study, PREPARE: Preparedness to Reduce Exposures and diseases Post-hurricanes & Augment Resilience and Oral Microbiome, Nitric oxide Metabolism, and Oral and Cardiometabolic Health.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/kaumudi-joshipura/|title=Kaumudi Joshipura|last=|first=|date=|website=Harvard School of Public Health|language=en-us|access-date=2019-07-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://vslir.iima.ac.in:8080/jspui/handle/11718/18855|title=Health Care Management: Think Outside Disease Care, for NCD Prevention across the Lifespan}}</ref>
